newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Sept trade balance shows $6.2 mln surplus.
newsitem.headline: Romania Sept trade balance shows $6.2 mln surplus.

text.p: Romania's trade balance had a $6.2 million surplus in September, recovering from $37.6 million deficit in August amid a 6.5 percent drop in last month's imports, National Statistics Board (CNS) data showed.
Romanian exports slipped by 1.1 percent in September from the previous month, but they were up 13.9 percent year-on-year, a CNS report said on Monday.
Over January-September, exports fell by 5.5 percent from the same period a year ago and imports were 11.1 percent down.
Common metals and textiles took some 36 percent of nine- month exports, while minerals accounted for 25.7 percent of Romanian imports, CNS data showed.
Some 54 percent of nine-month exports went to European Union countries, also the source of more than half of Romania's imports. Germany was Romania's main trading partner.

NOTES -- All figures in FOB prices. The CNS 1996 import data include oil imports on which custom documents were delayed in August but do not include oil imports on which custom papers were not cleared by the end of September.
